hero.heading: Neural-data law, row by row.
hero.lede: Which laws touch neural data, how each one defines it, and where each statement comes from. The table is generated from the same rule files the platform uses to classify channels. Rows whose source we could not verify are marked unverified.

rows.status: Status of each bill not verified
rows.text: Peer-reviewed reviews list bills under consideration in Alabama, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Illinois and Vermont.
rows.note: Named in reviews only; the bills and their status were not opened.

rows.instrument: MIND Act of 2025 (Management of Individuals' Neural Data)
rows.status: Introduced September 2025; bill number, sponsors and current status not verified
rows.text: The bill defined neural data and directed the Federal Trade Commission to study how to regulate it.
rows.note: That the bill was introduced is reported in a peer-reviewed article; its number, sponsors and current status were not opened.

rows.text: No federal statute regulates neural data; federal governance of neurotechnology is mostly soft policy.

HIPAA applies to covered entities and their business associates. Many consumer, wellness and research-only neurotech companies are not covered entities, so state privacy laws are their binding constraint.
rows.note: The second sentence is our reading of scope, not legal advice.

rows.text: Bans AI systems that infer emotions of people in workplace and education settings, except for medical or safety reasons.
rows.note: Cited from a secondary site that reproduces the article text (grade B).

rows.text: Protects cerebral activity and the information drawn from it; in 2023 the Supreme Court ordered neural-data deletion.
